bluf: Hero Digital is a US web, CX and product agency whose domain now redirects to hugeinc.com: a November 2025 Huge release cites Huge's integration with Hero Digital, and Hero Digital job ads still ran on LinkedIn in September 2026. The record holds no standalone positioning, services, clients, capability scores, Horus read or Monsoon read for it; what the domain serves is Huge's site, a human first, AI native design and technology company. A rival should know this is a brand in transition with no public record left to weigh: clients that signed with Hero Digital are now Huge clients, and the record is silent on which ones they are.
doing:
There is no Hero Digital positioning line to decode. The record states that the domain serves Huge's site, which describes itself as a human first, AI native design and technology company, so any positioning a buyer meets at herodigital.com is Huge's, not Hero Digital's. The record lists no headline claim, no services, no proprietary products, no partners, no verticals and no capability scores; the focus table is empty and no line is marked lead or core. The Radar files the segment as Web, CX & product in the US region, with ownership unknown, no founding year and no headcount.

The AI posture is silent for Hero Digital itself; the only AI language in the record is Huge's AI native self description on the successor site. Pricing signals are absent.

The one dated move is the merger: a November 2025 Huge release cites Huge's integration with Hero Digital, and herodigital.com now redirects to hugeinc.com. The status note adds that Hero Digital job ads still ran on LinkedIn in September 2026, which means the name was still being used to recruit well after the integration release, or the ads were left running; the record does not say which. The record lists no news items, no case studies and no jobs beyond those ad captures.

What is conspicuously absent is everything a web, CX and product agency normally shows: a work page, a client list, a platform partner badge, a services page and a team page. For a rival that absence is the finding: there is no Hero Digital offer left in public to compete against, only Huge's, and the question of which Hero Digital clients and staff moved across is unanswered on this record.
clients:
The needs read counts 0 clients for Hero Digital: no case studies, no press releases, no client slugs, so there is no observed need, no named only count, no mix and no shared client on record. The Radar files no client type, no verticals and no home market beyond the US region. The record says nothing about who Hero Digital worked for, in which industries, or what they came for.

The silence has a cause the record does state: herodigital.com redirects to hugeinc.com, so the pages that would have carried a work section or a client list were not captured under the Hero Digital name, and the successor site's clients are Huge's, not attributed to Hero Digital in this record. The Radar does not read the Huge book as the Hero Digital book.

What the base needs next cannot be tied to the edition's key judgments, because the record holds no Horus read for Hero Digital and no capability scores to drive one. The only judgment available concerns the transition: it is likely, with low confidence, that former Hero Digital clients are now served under the Huge brand for web build and platform work, the segment the Radar files it under, and it is a roughly even chance that some of those relationships were not carried across, since the record shows the name still recruiting on LinkedIn in Sept 2026 while the domain already redirected. A rival that wants the list has to build it from outside this record, and the record cannot confirm a single name.
house: The Radar ran no say and do test on Hero Digital, because no capability was scored; the house data it captured belongs to the successor site. The sitemap lists 93 URLs, with 11 updated in 90 days and 11 in 365, and 0 AI related URLs. There is no llms.txt and no AI crawler is blocked. The CMS is Next.js and the tag stack is GTM, sixsense and OneTrust, with sixsense the one ABM tool and no social pixel or test tool listed. The Google Transparency Center status is none, with 0 ads. LinkedIn is the one live signal: 3 company page ads under the Hero Digital name, from 20 ads matching the name query, with a second pass finding 3 dynamic job and follower ads; the sample reads, explore jobs at Hero Digital that match your skills. The social links point to Huge accounts on LinkedIn, Instagram and X, not to Hero Digital accounts.
market:
The record holds no Horus read for Hero Digital: with no capability scores, the edition's tailwind index, band, key judgment fit, scenario fit and P move status were not computed, so there is no figure to quote and no judgment it is best placed for or most exposed to. The same is true of the Monsoon read: no index, no band, no migration or displacement figure, no shore split and no delivery footprint, observed or inferred.

What can be said as a read is limited to the segment. The Radar files Hero Digital under Web, CX & product in the US, the segment the edition's key judgments touch through web build and platform hours; without scores the dossier cannot say whether those hours sit with the judgments or against them. Any market read a strategist wants on this name is, in effect, a read on Huge. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence: the record does not say Hero Digital had no offshore delivery or no AI line, only that nothing was captured.
openings:
The only computed opening is the transition. Brand status is merged: herodigital.com redirects to hugeinc.com, a November 2025 Huge release cites the integration, and Hero Digital job ads still ran on LinkedIn in September 2026. Clients in a transition answer the phone. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that former Hero Digital accounts in web, CX and product work are contestable during the fold into Huge, because the name they bought from no longer has a site, a work page or a positioning of its own. The falsifier is a Huge page that lists the former Hero Digital clients and case studies under the Huge brand with continuity of team, which would show the transition was managed and the accounts retained.

There is no contradiction to lead with, no gap the Radar flagged and no pricing exposure, because there is no sold mix on record to contradict. The offer that undercuts it is therefore not a cheaper line item but certainty: a rival pitching the same web build and platform work can say plainly who it is, what it sells and what it charges, none of which the Hero Digital name can now say in public.

Any Huge page or release that lists former Hero Digital clients: it is the falsifier for the transition opening and the only route to a client book on this record.
